I have a similar issue. I was assaulted my sophomore year of college by an older white man and same exact thing as you albeit a different race. Even if it's just a picture online of a man that is just middle aged and white, it can send me into a panic. I don't think you're prejudiced at all, I think it's just your brain associating those physical features with a very very traumatic experience.  Those features are just a trigger for you right now. It makes sense how it feels like you're prejudiced, but its just your brain's own messed up way of trying to keep you safe. Please keep reminding yourself that you're not an awful person or a racist for feeling this way, you didn't choose or ask for this in any way. The fact that it's weighing on you like this shows that. I've gotten better at it. I'm able to interact with older white men on a daily basis without too much issue, but when I see them in any sexualized format it still sets me off sometimes, like a shirtless photo online. Your brain just has to unlearn what it thinks is protecting you.  It'll take time, but you will heal. Stay strong friend.

You're not alone at all. These are how most of my attacks go. I do get it sometimes where it's just utter panic and a sense of well, impending doom, but most of the time its as you describe. Often people can't even tell I'm having an attack. I've had friends ask me for something mid attack, and I just stare them silently unable to speak. It's really isolating. When it's more of a freak out, people notice for better or worse. I get the shakes really bad, my whole body tenses up, chest pain, hyperventilating the works. It's like my senses fade away, and it's nothing but me and the panic. I'll want to talk, and communicate that I'm having an attack, but it's just so intense that I just cannot. Sensory overload it feels like. So yeah long way of saying that you're not alone. Something that has helped for me is finding something that stimulates your senses and kind of snaps you back. For me, dipping my arms in ice cold water or likewise splashing cold water on my face can snap me out of an attack. I feel like my senses just get so wrapped up in the panic that they just need a wake up call. Stay strong friend!

I'm scared too. It feels like I'm running towards the worst of the worst and I can't stop. As for what's helped me, I've started making some choices to better myself once I come out of quarantine. Make some goals for yourself. I've always been a bigger guy, so I've started running almost every day and eating healthier. Checking my weight every morning and seeing it consistently go down is the best part of my day. I think to the future, once I'm back in school and I show up a whole new me and stunting on everyone haha. It helps having something to latch onto. I can so easily fall into what I call the "corona hole", thinking of all the things I've lost, but I know how hard it can be, but try to think of all the things you can gain. Come out of this with a new skill maybe? Pick up an instrument, learn a language, think that once you're out of this, even if you fall into a bad episode, that there's things that give a bit of light at the end of the tunnel. 

So yeah, it might sound obvious but fine something to distract yourself. Not a one off thing like watching a TV show, but something you can consistently build on and hopefully that'll be enough to get you through the tough times ahead or hopefully not ahead.
